question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate indicates a high likelihood (95%) of at least 1,000 Mediterranean deaths by end-April 2026 or May 1, 2026, given a strong early pace.
Adversarial objections identify plausible downside risks: March–April slowdown from weather, reporting anomalies, and policy/SAR improvements that could reduce fatalities.
Threshold arithmetic shows hitting 1,000 by end-April requires roughly 394 deaths in March–April; this is plausible but not guaranteed given seasonal variability.
Calibrated probability is modestly adjusted downward from the ensemble to reflect downside risks while preserving high overall likelihood.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal genuine upside/downside uncertainty; none rely on physically implausible scenarios, so they warrant a calibrated adjustment rather than a dismissal.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted probability from 0.95 to 0.92 to incorporate plausible downside risks (March–April slowdown, reporting variability, SAR improvements). The range 0.86–0.98 is provided to capture remaining uncertainty.
